RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the February 20, 2009/Phalguna 1, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries:  Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
29
Export of sugar
*81. DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government plans to check
sugar exports via advance licence;
(b) if so, whether under this licence
scheme sugar millers will have to obtain
his Ministry's release orders  for shipping
out any consignment;
(c) whether India is still facing shortage
of sugar;
(d) whether Government is also
planning to extend Release Orders (RO)
dispensation to cover re-export
commitments under Advance Licence (AL)
scheme and the scheme also requires mills
to re-export one tonne of white sugar for
every 1.05 tonnes of raw-sugar they import
duty free; and
(e) if so, to what extent it has helped to
check sugar exports?
National Mission on Medicial Plants
*82. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has recently
approved a Centrally sponsored National
Mission on Medicinal Plants;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether most of the medicinal
plants are on the verge of extinction and
herbal industry has been affected adversely;
and
(d) if so, the facts thereof and the steps
taken by Government to encourage farmers
to grow more medicinal plants to protect
the herbal industry?
Export of wheat
*83. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISRIBUTION be
pleased to state:
(a) whether United States' Department

30
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
of Agriculture has gone ahead to project
that India may ease nearly two year old
ban on wheat shipment in May and even
use its large central reserve for exporting
the foodgrains after the rabi harvest;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) how it would be useful to our
country especially for the farmers of Andhra
Pradesh?
Pressure of passengers at railway
stations
*84. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the strength
of daily railway passengers from Agartala
to Dharmanagar is exceedingly high and
beyond the present in-take capacity of the
trains;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
ticket booking system prior to departure
of the trains at Agartala and other major
stations cannot cope with the pressure of
passengers; and
(c) if so, the remedy for the solution of
the problems outlined above?
Sick small scale industries
*85. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the
Minister of MICRO, SMALL AND
MEDIUM ENTERPRISES be pleased to
state:
(a) what was the total number of small
scale industries existing when the present
Government took over;
(b) how many of them have been newly
registered during the tenure of present
Government upto 31st March, 2008;
(c) how many units have been closed
during the tenure of present Government
till 31st March, 2008;
(d) how many of them have been revived
and restored;
(e) why the progress of revival and
rehabilitation of sick units was very slow;
and
(f) whether there would be a new
package and all out effort to deal with the
problem of closure of these units?
Infected ice-creams
†*86. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that according to
the Indian Council of Medical Research,
the tests of samples of ice-creams have
been found infected;
(b) if so, the number of samples taken
and how many of them were found infected,
and the details thereof; and
(c) the efforts being made to improve
the quality of ice-creams?
Substandard drugs
*87. SHRI A. ELA V ARASAN: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that many drugs
produced by the well known pharma
companies are substandard;
(b) if so, whether Government has
conducted any survey to find out the
quality of medicines produced by well
known, leading pharma companies;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) the action taken by Government

31
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
against those companies whose products
were found substandard?
Violation of PNDT Act
*88. SHRIMATI BRINDA KARA T:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the number of female foetuses
aborted in the country in violation of
Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques  (PNDT)
Act in last two years, State-wise; and
(b) the details of action taken by
Government in this regard?
Purchase of AK-47 rifles
†*89. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that his Ministry
has decided to buy three thousand AK-47
rifles;
(b) whether these would be given to
Railway Protection Force or a special force
would be formed; and
(c) the areas in which these are
proposed to be deployed?
Use of toxic chemicals in food and
vegetables
†*90. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether toxic chemicals are being
used in fresh foodstuff and sweets;
(b) whether Formaldehyde, Boric and
Benzoic acids, industrial colour sulphur
dioxide etc. are being used fearlessly in order
to keep vegetables fresh in look and colour;
(c) whether  use of these chemicals is
increasing liver, kidney and cancer related
diseases along with mental retardation and
hinders the physical and mental growth of
children;
(d) whether gas is used for making wine,
and also for ripening and drying of fruits,
which is increasing respiratory and heart
related diseases; and
(e) if so, the measures being taken to
stop this practice at processing and
marketing levels?
Production of wheat
*91. SHRIMATI MAY A SINGH: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that production
of wheat is sufficient to meet the
requirement of wheat eaters;
(b) if not, whether steps are being taken
to ensure enhanced production; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
expenditure incurred/likely to be incurred
thereon?
Proposals for railway projects from
Andhra Pradesh
*92. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of the proposals for
laying new lines/gauge conversion/
upgradation of stations/construction of
over or under bridges, received from Andhra
Pradesh Government during the last one
year and till date in current year;
(b) the status of clearance/
implementation of each of these proposals;
and

32
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) the time by when all these proposals
are likely to be implemented?
Foreign assistance for health projects
*93. SHRI RAJEEV CHANDRA-
SEKHAR: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) the total foreign assistance received
by India during 2008-09 for health projects,
indicating the source, the quantum and the
specific project in each case; and
(b) the extent of utilization of the funds
so far in each case along with the share of
the Union Government, if any, for the
same?
Railway Zone Advisory Committee
†*94. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether there is any fixed time period
to hold meetings of Railway Zone Advisory
Committee;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether the meeting of South
Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL) Railway
Zone Advisory Committee, Headquarter,
Mumbai is organizing its meetings regularly
at prescribed intervals; and
(d) if so, the details of meetings held by
Advisory Committee during the last two
years?
Terrorist attacks on stations and trains
*95. SHRI NAND KISHORE
Y ADAV:
SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR:
Will the Minister of RAILWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) the details of the terrorist  attacks
and bomb blasts that took place on various
railway stations and trains during the last
three years, zone and division-wise, till date;
(b) the details of the people injured and
killed in such activities during the last three
years, zone and division-wise, along with
the ex-gratia  payment to kins of the
deceased and the injured; and
(c) the details of security measures
taken/proposed to be taken to prevent
recurrence of such incidents in future?
Population control
*96. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the population in the
country is increasing rapidly and it is
expected to surpass the population of China;
(b) if so, whether in view of steep rise
in population, the Union Government
proposes to have a fresh look at our
Population Policy;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether the Union Government
proSposes to discuss the issue with the
State Governments/UTs to effectively
implement the Population Policy; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Undue delay in getting various
permission and pending applications
*97. DR. V . MAITREYAN: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether even after streamlining the
system of operations and inducting more
personnel, DCGI office is not able to

33
approve applications by the prescribed
deadline;
(b) if so, reasons therefor;
(c) whether the present DCGI goes on
frequent tours and has not delegated the
powers of approval to his subordinate
officials causing undue delay;
(d) if so, the immediate action proposed
to put the system on fast track;
(e) the number of applications as of
January 31, 2009 pending in each category
of approvals and how many have been
cleared; and
(f) whether there is also selective
amnesia in the department to clear only a
few applications?
Financial assistance for
District Hospitals, Primary
Health Centres etc.
*98. SHRI SHANTARAM LAXMAN
NAIK: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has any
schemes to give financial assistance in terms
of loans, grants etc. for construction/
maintenance/upgradation of District
Hospitals and Primary Health Centres in
the States;
(b) if so, the names of such schemes;
(c) the essential features of these
schemes;
(d) the financial assistance provided to
Government of Goa, if any, in the last three
years; and
(e) whether any proposal for financial
assistance in this regard is pending with
Government?
Storage facility of foodgrains
*99. SHRI KALRAJ MISHRA: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the report in the Tribune,
dated 24th December, 2008 that thousands
of tonnes of wheat procured under the
procurement programme continues to rot
in the open;
(b) if so, the steps taken by Government
to ensure that adequate storage facility is
provided to such foodgrains; and
(c) the details of Government's
assessment about the extent of inadequacy
of storing space for the procured grain with
procurement agencies in the country?
Market intelligence to farmers
for obtaining remunerative
price
*100. SHRIMATI RENUBALA
PRADHAN:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government of Orissa had
submitted a memorandum to the Union
Government to provide market intelligence
to the farmers to help them to get
remunerative prices for their agricultural
produce especially in the tribal dominated
Kandhamal district of the State;
(b) if so, the details thereof, alongwith
the status of the proposal;

34
(c) whether a demand has also been
made for setting up an Indian Council of
Agricultural Research (ICAR) unit in the
region to study and solve the problems now
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 14th February, 2009 Secretary-General.
Magha 25, 1930 (Saka)
being faced by the farmers; and
(d) if so, the details thereof along with
status of the proposal?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Agriculture : 91, 100,
Chemicals and Fertilizers : —
Consumer Affairs, Food and
Public Distribution : 81, 83, 99,
Health and Family Welfare : 82, 86, 87, 88, 90, 93, 96, 97, 98,
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises : 85,
Railways : 84, 89, 92, 94, 95.
Steel : —
35
MGIPMRND—548RS—14.02.2009.
